Open the starter project

Goal: you have the starter files open in Visual Studio Code and the page shows in your browser.
  1. Unzip the file you received from your teacher.
  2. In VS Code choose File ▸ Open Folder and select the unzipped folder.
  3. Right-click index.html and choose Open with Live Server. If you don’t see it, install the Live Server extension first.

Your folder should look like this:

You will only edit index.html and js/script.js. The CSS is already done.

Get your API key

Goal: you have a personal TMDB API key (a long code of letters and numbers).

An API is a web address that returns data instead of a web page. TMDB (The Movie Database) gives you data about movies, but it wants to know who is asking. That is what the key is for.

  1. Go to themoviedb.org and create an account (or log in).
  2. Open your profile menu ▸ Settings ▸ API.
  3. Click Create, choose Developer, and accept the terms.
  4. Fill in the form. What you type is not important, even the URL can be made up.
  5. Click Submit. Copy the API Key (v3 auth) and keep it for later.
I don’t want to register

Your script.js already contains a working key from your teacher, so you can continue without one. A personal key is still the better habit.

Build one movie card

Goal: the page shows three cards. Hover over a card to slide up the overview.

Open index.html. Inside <main> there is already one card. Copy it so you have three cards, and give the rating span of each card a different class: red, orange and green.

This is the template for every card the program will build later. Each card needs an image, a title, a rating and an overview.

📷 Show screenshots (click a picture to enlarge)

Know your three constants

Goal: you understand what each line at the top of script.js does. Nothing to type here.
  • API_URL is the endpoint for the most popular movies. discover/movie is the endpoint, sort_by=popularity.desc sorts it and page=1 asks for the first page.
  • IMG_PATH is the start of every image address. The data only contains the end part (like /sv1xJUaz….jpg). You change w1280 to w500 for smaller images.
  • SEARCH_API is the endpoint for searching. The search word is added at the end.

Paste the same key in both api_key= places if you made your own.

Paste API_URL into your browser’s address bar. You will see a wall of text. That is the data we will use next.

The Console shows an error
  • 401 Unauthorized: your API key is wrong. Copy it again, without spaces.
  • getMovie is not defined: check the spelling, including the capital M.
  • Nothing happens: check that index.html has <script src="js/script.js"> at the bottom.

Challenges

Goal: change the app on your own. Pick at least one.
  1. Use w500 instead of w1280 in IMG_PATH. What changes?
  2. Show the top rated movies. Look for the endpoint in the Discover examples on the TMDB site.
  3. Change page=1 to page=2. Then add a Next button.
  4. Some movies have no poster (poster_path is null). Show image/Myimage.jpg for those.
Extra: the same request with .then()

.then runs when the request succeeds. .catch runs when it fails.

Well done, you built a real app with live data. 🎉
